conceptual assets.reasoning: The RTL implements an on-chip register file signal reg_file that holds processor registers and is updated from the write-data input rd_i. In the FPGA path a clocked write does 'if (rf_we = '1') then reg_file(to_integer(unsigned(opa_addr(addr_bits_c-1 downto 0)))) <= rd_i;'. In the ASIC path each entry is clocked and updated when 'unsigned(ctrl_i.rf_rd(...)) = to_unsigned(i,...)' and 'ctrl_i.rf_wb_en = '1'' causing 'reg_file(i) <= rd_i;'. Those same reg_file entries feed read outputs (rs1_o <= reg_file(...); rs2_o <= reg_file(...)), so corruption of reg_file entries directly breaks read/write flows. reg_file is therefore the storing element for this value and rd_i is the input that sets stored values.

conceptual assets.concept: Register access control — the computed decision which register index is targeted and whether a write occurs
conceptual assets.reasoning: The RTL computes and enforces the register-access decision that determines which reg_file entry, if any, is updated. In the FPGA path rd_zero is computed ('rd_zero <= '1' when (ctrl_i.rf_rd = "00000") else '0';'), rf_we is computed ('rf_we <= (ctrl_i.rf_wb_en and (not rd_zero)) or ctrl_i.rf_zero_we;') and the target index is chosen by opa_addr ('opa_addr <= "00000" when (ctrl_i.rf_zero_we = '1') else ctrl_i.rf_rd when (ctrl_i.rf_wb_en = '1') else ctrl_i.rf_rs1;') and the process writes using those signals. In the ASIC path the per-register process writes when 'unsigned(ctrl_i.rf_rd(...)) = to_unsigned(i,...)' and 'ctrl_i.rf_wb_en = '1''. These computations define who may write and which index is written; incorrect computation or tampering would permit or prevent writes improperly, establishing an Integrity objective for access control. The decision is realized by rf_we and rd_zero (computes) and by opa_addr (computes); the control bus entering the entity (ctrl_i) supplies the inputs used to compute these decisions (sets).

conceptual assets.concept: Register read outputs delivered on rs1_o and rs2_o
conceptual assets.reasoning: The RTL drives the module read outputs from reg_file entries on clock edges: FPGA path assigns 'rs1_o <= reg_file(to_integer(unsigned(opa_addr(...)))); rs2_o <= reg_file(to_integer(unsigned(ctrl_i.rf_rs2(...))));' and ASIC path assigns 'rs1_o <= reg_file(to_integer(unsigned(ctrl_i.rf_rs1(...)))); rs2_o <= reg_file(...)' in the clocked read process. These outputs leave the entity and consumers depend on their correctness; thus integrity of the reported read values is established. The outputs themselves are the exit ports and reg_file is their stored source; ctrl_i supplies the read indices.
